context:
Treat this as a taxonomy and governance change first. Start from existing
documented commitments, then reconcile code evidence against those
commitments. Prefer a small, enforceable contract map over aspirational prose.
description:
BenchBox has several real product contracts that are only partially declared:
CLI behavior, Python wrappers, BaseBenchmark.run_with_platform, adapter
subclassing, MCP tools, result JSON, explorer input, generated compatibility
docs, platform availability, and experimental modules. The architecture is
still sound, but future work is making contract decisions implicitly.

This item creates one authoritative map of public/stable, beta-public,
internal, experimental, deprecated, generated, and repo-only surfaces. It also
defines support status vocabulary for platforms and benchmarks so docs,
registry metadata, packaging, MCP, and PR review use the same language.

anti_patterns.dont: collapse wrappers into internals just because they duplicate CLI reachability
anti_patterns.instead: classify them first, then decide deprecation separately.
anti_patterns.why: tests assert wrapper facades as public behavior

anti_patterns.instead: generate docs from registry metadata or fail the drift check.

anti_patterns.why: ambiguous tiers recreate the same blind spot
